With NTCT pre-cutoff drawdown of -33.4% and Goodwill = 61% of total assets, the gap between market cap and book equity is the cross-check the 10-K does not present.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Book equity at FY23 close: ~$2.03B on ~71.25M shares = book value per share ~$28.50. Q3 FY24 10-Q (filed Feb 2024) reversed course: 'As a result of the sustained decline in the Company's stock price and overall market capitalization during the third quarter of fiscal year 2024 ... it was determined a triggering event occurred ... recorded a goodwill impairment charge of $167.1 million during the periods ended December 31, 2023.' Goodwill written down from $1.724B (Mar 2023) to ~$1.557B (Dec 2023). Quantitative test used 'market approach' with a 'company-specific control premium' as the key assumption — a discretionary input.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catches the asymmetry the FY2023 10-K does not address: $1.72B of goodwill (61% of assets, 85% of book equity) supported by a Step-0 qualitative assessment in a year when the stock price had already declined meaningfully toward the triggering threshold. The Q2 FY24 10-Q (filed 5 months later) doubled down on Step-0 even after disclosing 'late in the second quarter' order conversion slowdown. The Q3 FY24 reversal — $167.1M impairment plus explicit warning 'the Company may be required to record additional goodwill impairment charges' — confirms the FY2023 10-K Step-0 election was at minimum optimistically timed. Forensic priority signal: the impairment finally taken at Dec 2023 still leaves $1.56B of goodwill carried at a control-premium-dependent valuation.

The framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline catches that the FY23 10-K should have characterized the RF-propagation bulge as project-driven (mention is present in the MD&A 10% increase in product revenue) but did not pair it with concentration risk disclosure about durability.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify that 'precautionary actions' actually appear as line items (restructuring charges, headcount reduction); Mode B — derive: if 'slowing in order conversion' is severe enough to require disclosure under SOX going-concern evaluation framing AND severe enough to trigger goodwill impairment one quarter later, the 'managing discretionary spending and hiring activities' framing materially understates the action being taken.

Yet Q3 FY24 9-month G&A was $73.975M vs $75.584M prior year (-2.1%), R&D $117.655M vs $129.932M prior year (-9.4%), S&M $209.070M vs $209.435M (flat). R&D cut of -9.4% YoY with no restructuring charge implies attrition-driven workforce contraction. Net loss YTD Q3 FY24: -$115.3M vs +$62.9M prior year — a -$178M swing. The $167.1M goodwill impairment dominates the swing but operating loss ex-impairment was still -$112.85M operating loss for nine months YTD vs +$76.0M prior. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'managing discretionary spending and hiring activities' framing is technically accurate but understates the operating reality: R&D down 9% on attrition without a restructuring charge classification (which would otherwise force severance disclosure), share repurchases cut by two-thirds, and a deepening operating loss ex-impairment. Disclosure quality is borderline — the language passes a literal reading test but a Mode B investor reading should infer 'soft hiring freeze + attrition + buyback throttle' from the line-item moves rather than from the narrative.

summary: NetScout's pre-cutoff disclosure stack shows a clear three-quarter deterioration from a clean FY2023 10-K to a Q3 FY24 10-Q carrying a $167.1M goodwill impairment, 19% Q3 revenue decline, U.S. revenue down 32% YoY, an explicit forward warning of further possible goodwill impairments, and small post-disclosure insider sales by the COO and EVP World-Wide Sales. The Mode-B forensic findings are (a) the FY2023 10-K's qualitative Step-0 goodwill assessment was optimistically timed given that the same year's Verizon 10%+ revenue concentration was driven by a transient RF-propagation project that subsequently reverted, and (b) the residual $1.56B goodwill — still 60% of total assets — is valued via a discretionary control-premium assumption that the Q3 FY24 10-Q itself flags as at risk of further impairment. However, the framework's honesty-alpha lens correctly catches that NTCT is NOT a lying-distress profile: disclosure cadence was honest and contemporaneous (Q2 FY24 disclosed slowdown in real time, Q3 FY24 took the impairment promptly), the auditor (PwC, 30 years) is clean with unqualified ICFR opinion, the credit facility is genuinely benign ($700M undrawn revolver, 2026 maturity, no covenant relief required), and the substantial-doubt evaluation is supportable. The pre-cutoff -33.4% drawdown appears proportionate to the disclosed deterioration. Verdict: NEUTRAL leaning slightly NEGATIVE — the operating impairment is real and not fully baked into the residual goodwill, but the balance-sheet resilience and disclosure honesty do not support a SHORT-tier framework verdict. This is the SRPT pattern from prior calibration: re-detecting honestly disclosed bad news is not the framework's edge.
